subject: Availability variance on 2028-08-31 — credit eligibility & RCA scheduling
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orchardpay.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@orchardpay.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: sustained 503/timeout window during checkout (2028-08-31) — request for verification and credits

Hi Laura,

We observed a sustained set of 503s and timeouts from Redwood-hosted endpoints during our peak checkout period on 2028-08-31 between ~14:05 and 14:44 PDT. This caused a ~2.8% drop in successful transactions for that 40-minute window and triggered customer support escalations on our side.

Our SREs collected traces and a short timeline (attached). Can Redwood confirm whether this maps to an availability SLO breach for OrchardPay and advise on credit eligibility under our contract? We need an initial answer for our leadership call at 09:00 PT tomorrow.

Attachments: orchardpay_request_timeline_20280911.csv

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Integrations | OrchardPay
elena.ruiz@orchardpay.com
+1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Immediate: sustained 503/timeout window during checkout (2028-08-31) — request for verification and credits

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the timeline. We take these windows very seriously.

Quick notes / next steps: 
- I’ve looped in David (SRE) and Aditya (incident lead) to pull the raw telemetry and panoptic traces for US-WEST-2.
- Can you also attach the lightweight trace bundle and any client-side retry logs if available? That will help us validate the window boundaries.
- We will triage and provide an impact verification (downtime window start/end, affected routers/nodes) within our SLA response timeline — target: by 09:00 PT tomorrow.
- If we confirm entitlement, we’ll outline the credit calculation methodology (prorated based on affected tenant usage during the window) and propose a remediation/RCA meeting.

One operational ask: please confirm whether OrchardPay observed any divergent routing (e.g., sudden route to fallback region) or if all traffic was to our standard hosted endpoint.

I’ll follow up after David posts the initial window verification.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: sustained 503/timeout window during checkout (2028-08-31) — request for verification and credits

Hi Elena / Michael — thanks for the bundle. We completed the initial validation this morning. Summary below (high level):

- Impact window we verified: 2028-08-31 14:07:12 PDT -> 2028-08-31 14:42:53 PDT (35 minutes, 41 seconds).
- Root cause (short): transient routing instability caused a small set of cache nodes to evict and enter a degraded slow-path; requests to those shards returned 503s until the autoscaler/election stabilized.
- Affected tenants: OrchardPay traffic routed to shard group w-77. Our telemetry shows OrchardPay accounted for ~2.6% of total requests on w-77 during the window.

Next steps & credits:
1) Entitlement: based on the verified impact window and your contract SLO, OrchardPay is eligible for a pro-rata service credit. We’ll calculate the exact credit using the formula in section 4.2 of the contract (pro-rata by affected tenant request weight during the window).
2) Calculation: we expect to complete the detailed credit calculation and share the proposed credit amount by EOD PT on 2028-09-13 after cross-checking billing and request accounting.
3) RCA meeting: propose Wed 2028-09-13 08:00 PT for a 40-minute post-incident review. Agenda: technical sequence (10m), telemetry review (10m), remediation plan + mitigations (15m), credit methodology + timeline (5m). Please confirm availability.
4) Evidence pack: we’ll attach a raw trace bundle and our shard-level telemetry in the next email.

On the remediation side we’ve already scoped a short-term control to reduce eviction+slow-path coupling during autoscaler churn; longer-term we’ll propose an autoscaler stability patch and shard health metrics for customers.

Let me know if that cadence works for OrchardPay. We’ll treat the credit calculation and RCA as high priority.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
